system: Bot body, overhead health bar and hit flash
what: Builds each bot's soldier model for its faction and hangs a two-plane health bar over its head, coloured by relation to you (activateRoster: your team teal 0x38e1b0 on 0x08302a, other teams red 0xff4d4d on 0x300808). Each frame the bar faces the camera and shrinks with health, and the body flashes red for 0.12 s when hit.

v2_note: Keep the idea: a bar per soldier, a short flash on hit. Avoid one new bar geometry and material per bot, and a traverse with a closure that rewrites every mesh's emissive on each toggle (it also touches materials that may be shared). Use an instanced or batched bar and a per-instance flash uniform. The flash is part of the LOOP_V2 §7 target-flinch feedback.
reason: Client-side presentation of a soldier. Keep the technique (billboard bar, hit flash), not the look.

what: Every 0.25 s (staggered by slot) each bot looks for the nearest visible soldier of another team within 44 m, and re-checks its current target's sight every 0.1 s. All bots share one budget of sight checks per game second (480, banked up to 0.1 s). A scan that runs out resumes from a cursor on the next frame. The bot loop starts one slot later each step so no team is always served first.

system: Bot combat movement and melee lunge
what: With a visible target, the bot turns to face it, closes in through navSteer when farther than preferRange + 3 m, backs straight off when closer than preferRange - 3 m, and strafes sideways, switching direction every 1-2.5 s. Speed is 4.2 m/s times the unit's speedMult. The Warrior lunges for 48 melee damage within 3.2 m, on a 2.5 s cooldown.

Movement runs on variable frame dt (loop 3053, capped 0.05) with Math.random timers: v2 needs the fixed tick and a seeded RNG for deterministic replays.
reason: Bot movement and melee damage are mechanics the authoritative sim decides.

system: Bot roles, siege and objective behaviour
what: With no visible target, a bot acts by role, cycled per team slot (push, objective, hunt). Objective bots walk to the active Tech Box while their team doesn't hold it, and otherwise behave like push bots. Push bots head for the nearest live structure of their push team (rotated on each respawn; any other active team when that team has no live building), but still take another team's truck when it is nearer than that building and within 42 m. Hunt bots go for other teams' trucks first. Bots stop 15 m from a building or 13 m from a truck and fire at it, dealing a flat 11 damage with no hit test. Objective and siege walking uses the plain 4.2 m/s, without the unit's speedMult that combat movement applies.
where: shamble-game.js:1566-1572 nearestEnemyStructure (pushTeam, hunt, 42 m truck rule); 1582-1583 AI_STATE.rotatePush; role assignment in activateRoster 770 (TUNE.ai.roles core:104); 2914-2928 bot loop objective and siege branches (walk speed dt*T.enemyMoveSpeed at 2917, 2922, 2926 vs combat dt*T.enemyMoveSpeed*eu.speedMult at 2909; siege cadence T.enemyFireInterval*1.6 + up to 0.4 s at 2923, 2927); 1642-1649 siegeFire; 852-856 siegeFireHarvester; T.enemySiegeDamage 11, enemyFireInterval 0.22 shamble-core.js:79-80
evidence: three-teams-core report: reach.js siege chain Cabana 75 %, objective climbs 72.5 % (buildings aren't nav cells, R19), DM_Tri 100 %; seeded FX-cull logs include 26 building and 1 truck siege shot in 180 s. STATUS risk 1 (R19).
v2_note: Siege damage skips the shot system: no ray, no line of sight, flat damage. In v2, route structure damage through the same shots. LOOP_V2 §10 asks for a simple, observable role mix per team (for example 40 % centre, 30 % uplinks, 30 % harvesters) that rebalances when objectives change, and for bots that buy T1 units, escort and hunt harvesters, and carry, defend and steal uplinks. §4 replaces Tech Boxes and silos with uplinks. The nearest-target selection itself (indexed loops, no allocation) is worth keeping. Found in code: objective and siege walking ignores the unit speed multiplier (2917, 2922, 2926), so a fast unit slows to base speed when it has no target; in v2 one movement speed rule per unit.
reason: LOOP_V2 §10 (role mix, uplinks, harvester escort) and §4 (uplinks replace Tech Boxes and silos) replace these rules.

system: Bot verticality: climb steering, jumps and collision
what: In combat (only while a target is visible), when the target stands higher above the bot than it can jump (about 3.07 m), the bot walks to the low end of the nearest ramp, as long as the bot is below 0.8 m and more than 3.5 m from that low end. A bot jumps when the ground 1.5 m ahead is above a step but within jump reach. Then it is clamped to the arena, pushed out of obstacles at radius 0.7 m, and given gravity.
where: shamble-game.js:1575 EJUMP_REACH (T.jumpV²/(2·T.gravity)+T.stepUp); 1602-1606 enemyClimbSteer (rampLowEnd inlined); 2931 arena clamp; 2932 jump test (surfaceHeightAt); 2933 resolveObstacles(…,0.7) + tickVertical
evidence: None recorded for climb steering. reach.js 'climb' measures building roofs, not ramp use (three-teams-core report: Cabana objective climbs 72.5 %).
v2_note: enemyClimbSteer picks the nearest ramp by its centre, whether or not it leads to the target's ledge, and steers only while the bot is below 0.8 m. It ignores the nav grid, which has no height. In v2, give the nav graph heights and links (ramps, jumps) so A* plans the climb. The 0.7 m bot radius must match the nav clearance (GN11). Collision and gravity themselves (resolveObstacles, tickVertical) belong to the GW movement rows.
reason: Bot movement, collision and navigation are mechanics the authoritative sim decides.

what: Eight-neighbour A* with an octile heuristic and no corner cutting, on preallocated typed arrays with a search stamp, so a search allocates nothing. A blocked start or goal moves to the nearest open cell. The search gives up after 8,000 expansions. The path is string-pulled with a grid line-of-sight test, up to 24 cells ahead, into at most 64 waypoints.

v2_note: Keep: zero-allocation search with stamps, the octile heuristic, no corner cutting, the nearest-free snap, string-pulling. Avoid the 8,000 cap failing to a straight line (use hierarchical or flow-field paths for 48+ bots heading to shared goals). The warm-up exists only to stop V8 deoptimising navPath, so drop it in Rust.
reason: Bot navigation is decided by the authoritative sim; the algorithm ports directly.

system: Route following, replanning and route budget
what: navSteer walks a bot straight when the grid line to its goal is clear. Otherwise it follows a cached route, skipping waypoints it can see. It replans when it has no route, when the goal has moved more than 3 m, every 1.5 s, or when the bot has moved under 0.35 m in 0.8 s. At most 2 searches run per update across all bots.
where: shamble-game.js:2657-2670 navSteer (en._nav {pts Float32Array(128), n, i, gx, gz, t, chk, lx, lz, stuck}); 2671 NAV.budget=2 at the top of update(); callers 2907, 2917, 2922, 2926
evidence: bot-poplar-wedge report PERF-2: the replan storm, where a bot whose straight line flickers clear/blocked replans every few frames (budget-limited frames 0.9 % to 1.8 % on Romania); no other measurement of replanning is recorded. For route following in general, the same report's paired walks after the wedge fix (clearance and open start cell, not a replan change): stalls of 3 s or more 1-16 per set to 0, direction reversals 226-1,048 to 0-22. three-teams-core report: route denials 52-57 % at 48 soldiers. STATUS: replan storm queued as bot-replan-storm.
v2_note: Known bug: the replan storm (LOOP_V2 §10 says to fix it before uplinks, because moving objectives will make bots replan constantly; §11 step 4). Found in code: NAV.budget is reset on every update() call (2671), so route searches per second grow with frame rate, unlike the sight budget, which counts game time. In Rust, give it a budget per tick and a queue of fair requests, and hysteresis on the clear/blocked switch.
reason: Bot navigation is decided by the authoritative sim and LOOP_V2 keeps it (with the replan-storm fix).
